trust_decision.summary: When the `pattern` keyword's value is a $data reference, the regex source comes from the validated (untrusted) data. Generated code compiles it with native `new RegExp` and ignores the configured `code.regExp` engine (e.g. RE2), with no try/catch. The fix routes it through the configured engine and wraps it in try/catch.

landing_point.why: Summary says ReDoS with $data. The only $data-dependent RegExp construction in lib/ is this line, and it has a TODO about try/catch right above it.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API: new Ajv({$data: true}).compile(schema with pattern: {$data: ...}) then validate(data)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists. Every other RegExp construction in lib/ compiles a schema-author string, not data (lib/vocabularies/code.ts:95-104 already uses opts.code.regExp; lib/core.ts:650 and lib/vocabularies/applicator/patternProperties.ts:53 are schema-author/compile-time). The project documents schema regexes as the author's responsibility (docs/security.md:64-66).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valid $data patterns must still match correctly, with the unicode flag `u` still passed. If $data resolves to undefined, validation must still pass (fail$data semantics). The non-$data path must keep using usePattern/scopeValue so standalone code still works. An over-broad fix that rejects complex patterns or drops $data support for pattern would break these.

O6_input_shapes: $data pattern string with a catastrophic-backtracking regex (engine choice)
$data pattern string that is syntactically invalid (throws in RegExp constructor -> caught, valid=false)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a $data format path that builds a RegExp from a data-supplied string (e.g. when fDef is a string) instead of looking it up as a compiled format
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The $data format path already branches on RegExp vs object vs string and calls `${format}.test(${data})` at runtime. A maintainer could plausibly let string formats compile lazily there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: native `new RegExp(pat)` that bypasses opts.code.regExp, already present for the strict-mode check; a runtime copy over data keys would be a realistic second site
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Shows the codebase already mixes native RegExp with the configured engine. Today pat and prop are both schema-author values at compile time.

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm, tsc, mocha (spec/*.spec.ts); fix test imports dist/runtime/re2, which needs the native `re2` npm package built
O10_build.project_tests: spec/ (mocha), e.g. JSON-Schema-Test-Suite $data tests plus spec/issues/*; the fix adds spec/issues/cve_2025_69873_redos_attack.spec.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the existing `new RegExp(schemaCode)` in try/catch only, leaving the native backtracking engine in place, or reject 'unsafe-looking' patterns with a heuristic.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/core.ts:650 addFormat compiles string formats with native `new RegExp`, ignoring opts.code.regExp. The regex is schema-author controlled, not data, so it falls outside this advisory's property.
